title: Failure Recovery Runbook
purpose: Comprehensive runbook for recovering from common failure modes in the multi-agent coordination system. Covers agent crashes, SQLite lock contention, bus file corruption, coordinator failures, and network/resource failures. Each section provides detection, diagnosis, and recovery procedures with concrete commands.

agent_crash_recovery.title: Agent Crash Recovery
agent_crash_recovery.overview: Agents may crash due to errors, resource exhaustion, or timeout. Recovery involves detecting the crash via stale heartbeats, preserving any partial output, and relaunching with context.

detection.method: Monitor agent heartbeats via the coordinator hub. A heartbeat older than 2x the expected interval indicates a crash.
detection.command: python3 -c "from storage.coordination.coordinator_hub import CoordinatorHub; h = CoordinatorHub(); [print(f'{a[\"agent_id\"]}: last_heartbeat={a[\"last_heartbeat\"]}') for a in h.get_stale_agents(timeout_seconds=60)]"
indicators: Heartbeat timestamp older than 60 seconds (for 30s heartbeat interval)
Agent status shows 'registered' but no recent bus messages
Output file has not been updated despite agent being 'active'

steps.action: Check the agent's last bus messages for error indicators
Check for partial output from the crashed agent
Check system resources to rule out OOM or disk full
Deregister the stale agent from the coordinator
steps.command: python3 -c "from storage.coordination.coordinator_hub import CoordinatorHub; h = CoordinatorHub(); h.deregister_agent('<agent_id>')"

steps.action: Preserve any partial output by copying it to a backup location
Relaunch the agent with its original prompt plus context about what was already completed
steps.prompt_addition: NOTE: You are replacing a previous agent that crashed. Partial output from the previous run is at: <path>. Review it and continue from where it left off. Do not redo completed work.

steps.action: Verify the relaunched agent registers and begins sending heartbeats

recovery.if_repeated_crashes: If the same agent crashes more than twice on the same task: (1) Split the task into smaller subtasks, (2) Check for systematic issues like infinite loops or memory leaks, (3) Assign the task to a different team with adjusted instructions.

sqlite_lock_contention.title: SQLite Lock Contention
sqlite_lock_contention.overview: Multiple agents writing to the SQLite database simultaneously can cause lock contention. The system uses WAL mode and busy_timeout to mitigate this, but under heavy load, additional intervention may be needed.

measures.description: Write-Ahead Logging allows concurrent reads during writes
Set a timeout so writers wait instead of immediately failing on lock
Acquire write lock at transaction start to fail fast rather than at commit time
measures.pattern: Use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for all write transactions. Never use plain BEGIN for writes.

symptoms: Agents reporting write failures in bus messages
Slow agent registration or status updates
detection.interpretation: If WAL file is very large (>10MB), writes are backing up faster than checkpoints can flush them.

steps.action: Force a WAL checkpoint to flush pending writes
Increase busy_timeout if agents are timing out
steps.note: This is a per-connection setting. Each agent's Python code should also set it.

steps.action: Implement retry logic for BEGIN IMMEDIATE failures
If contention persists, stagger agent write operations by adding jitter
steps.technique: Each agent adds random.uniform(0, 0.5) seconds before writes to spread out lock acquisition

emergency.description: If the database is completely locked and no agents can write
steps: Restart agents one at a time with staggered startup (2s delay between each)

bus_file_corruption.title: Bus File Corruption
bus_file_corruption.overview: JSONL bus files can become corrupted if a write is interrupted mid-line (crash, disk full) or if atomic write guarantees are violated (message > 4096 bytes).

symptoms: JSON parse errors when reading bus messages
bus_cli.py crashes with 'Expecting value' or 'Extra data' errors
detection.diagnostic_command: python3 -c "import json; f=open('storage/coordination/bus/<channel>.jsonl'); [json.loads(l) for l in f]" 2>&1 | tail -5
detection.interpretation: A JSONDecodeError with a line number indicates exactly where corruption occurred.

steps.action: Try the built-in repair function first
steps.what_it_does: Reads each line, discards unparseable lines, writes clean lines to a new file, replaces the original.

steps.action: If repair_bus_file is unavailable, manually repair
commands:
python3 -c "
import json
clean_lines = []
with open('storage/coordination/bus/<channel>.jsonl.corrupt_backup') as f:
    for line in f:
        try:
            json.loads(line.strip())
            clean_lines.append(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            pass
with open('storage/coordination/bus/<channel>.jsonl', 'w') as f:
    f.writelines(clean_lines)
print(f'Recovered {len(clean_lines)} messages')
"

steps.action: If the file is beyond repair or most messages are lost, backup and recreate
steps.warning: This loses all historical messages on this channel. Only do this as a last resort.

steps.action: Notify affected teams via a working channel that the corrupted channel has been repaired/reset
steps.command: python3 storage/coordination/bus_cli.py send global --type info --body 'Channel <channel> was repaired. Some messages may have been lost. Re-send any critical pending messages.'

prevention: Keep messages under 4096 bytes to ensure atomic POSIX writes
Monitor disk space: df -h . (corruption risk increases when disk is >90% full)
Use the bus_cli.py for all bus writes instead of direct file I/O

coordinator_failure.title: Coordinator Failure
coordinator_failure.overview: If the coordinator hub process crashes or hangs, agents lose their central monitoring point. Recovery involves detecting the failure, preserving state, and restarting.

detection.method: The multi_team_runner.py includes a watchdog that monitors the coordinator's heartbeat.
indicators: Agents cannot register or update status
No new entries in the coordinator's SQLite tables
detection.manual_check: python3 -c "from storage.coordination.coordinator_hub import CoordinatorHub; h = CoordinatorHub(); print(h.get_hub_status())"

steps.action: Preserve the current database state before any recovery action
Verify database integrity
Restart the coordinator hub
steps.note: The hub will re-read state from SQLite. Agent registrations persist across restarts.

steps.action: Verify agents reconnect and heartbeats resume
steps.command: python3 -c "from storage.coordination.coordinator_hub import CoordinatorHub; h = CoordinatorHub(); agents = h.list_agents(); print(f'{len(agents)} agents registered'); [print(f'  {a[\"agent_id\"]}: {a[\"status\"]}') for a in agents]"

steps.action: If agents do not reconnect within 30 seconds, re-register them manually
steps.command: python3 -c "from storage.coordination.coordinator_hub import CoordinatorHub; h = CoordinatorHub(); h.register_agent('<agent_id>', '<team_name>')"

if_state_lost.description: If the database is corrupted and no backup exists
steps: Create a fresh database: rm storage/coordination/db/state.db && python3 -c "from storage.coordination.coordinator_hub import CoordinatorHub; CoordinatorHub()"
Re-register all active agents from bus message history
Reconstruct team assignments from team output directories
Resume operations — agents continue working even without coordinator monitoring

network_resource_failures.title: Network and Resource Failures
network_resource_failures.overview: External API calls, web searches, and resource-intensive operations can fail due to network issues, rate limits, or resource exhaustion. Use exponential backoff with jitter for all retries.

connection_timeout.symptom: ConnectionError or TimeoutError after long wait

rate_limit_429.action: Respect Retry-After header if present. Otherwise, backoff starting at 5 seconds.
rate_limit_429.note: Do not treat 429 as an error — it is a signal to slow down

server_error_5xx.action: Retry with exponential backoff. These are usually transient.

disk_full.symptom: OSError: No space left on device
disk_full.action: Do NOT retry. Clean up disk space first.
cleanup_commands: Remove old bus files: find storage/coordination/bus/ -name '*.jsonl' -mtime +1 -exec rm {} \;

out_of_memory.symptom: MemoryError or process killed by OOM killer
out_of_memory.action: Reduce batch sizes, process data in chunks, or split the task across more agents

circuit_breaker.description: If an external service fails repeatedly, stop trying and fail fast instead of wasting time on retries.
circuit_breaker.trigger: 5 consecutive failures to the same endpoint within 2 minutes
circuit_breaker.action: Mark the service as 'down' and skip all requests to it for 5 minutes
circuit_breaker.recovery: After 5 minutes, attempt a single probe request. If it succeeds, resume normal operation. If it fails, extend the cooldown to 15 minutes.

agent_crash: Check last bus messages for error context
Relaunch with context about prior progress
Verify new agent registers and heartbeats
sqlite_lock: Force WAL checkpoint if WAL file is large
Verify BEGIN IMMEDIATE is used for writes
Add jitter to write operations if contention persists
Emergency: stop all agents, checkpoint, integrity check, staggered restart
bus_corruption: Identify corrupted channel from error messages
Manual repair if repair function unavailable
Backup and recreate as last resort
Verify channel is functional after repair
coordinator_failure: If state lost: recreate DB, re-register from bus history
network_resource: Check if circuit breaker should trigger
For disk full: clean up old files before retrying
For OOM: reduce batch size or split task
Log all failures for post-operation review

quick_reference.agent_crash: Detect stale heartbeat → deregister → backup partial output → relaunch with context
quick_reference.sqlite_lock: Verify WAL + busy_timeout → checkpoint → retry with BEGIN IMMEDIATE → add jitter
quick_reference.bus_corruption: repair_bus_file → manual repair → backup and recreate → notify teams
quick_reference.coordinator_down: Backup DB → integrity check → restart hub → verify reconnection
quick_reference.network_failure: Exponential backoff with jitter → circuit breaker after 5 failures → fail fast and report
